summary: Keep Leaflet 1.9.4 (BSD-2, 42 KB gz, classic UMD) as the primary map engine and add ECharts 6.1 geo as the second. Both are already vendored. Leaflet 2.0 is still only 2.0.0-alpha.1 (Aug 2025), with no beta or rc. It drops factory methods, and in my test the 1.x plugins broke: the V1 polyfill rescued leaflet.heat and markercluster, but not leaflet-ant-path. I ran 17 offline tests (pages opened via file:// in headless Chromium, outbound requests blocked). They passed for Leaflet with its plugins, ECharts, deck.gl 9.4 UMD, OpenLayers 10.11, Observable Plot, MapLibre 5.24 UMD and AntV L7. L7 is the exception on network calls: it fetches its logo from gw.alipayobjects.com unless logoVisible:false. MapLibre 6 (July 2026) is ESM-only and WebGL2-only, and Chrome blocks it under file:// with a CORS error. 5.24.0 is the last UMD build and is now frozen. It still works offline with inline GeoJSON and with in-memory PMTiles via addProtocol, and draws labels with local fonts when glyph files can't load. Critical bug: world-atlas TopoJSON is spherical and stitched across the date line, so every planar renderer draws horizontal streaks from Russia, Fiji and Antarctica. Only d3 and Observable Plot draw it cleanly. Fix: cut the polygons at ±180°. In JS this is d3.geoProject with an identity equirectangular projection (verified: 7 to 0 jumps in 25 ms), but it is better done once in the Python builder. world-atlas is also archived, still on Natural Earth 4.1.0, and its 110m file has no Singapore, Hong Kong, Macao, Bahrain, Malta, Cayman or Bermuda. Rebuild the basemap from Natural Earth 5.1.2 10m simplified 1% with keep-shapes: about 109 KB, keeps these micro-states, and allows China point-of-view boundaries. Join on ISO_A3_EH or ADM0_A3, because ISO_A3 is -99 for France and Norway. Verified ECharts features worth reusing: pies placed on geo coordinates (replaces the GPL leaflet.minichart), heatmap on geo, brush selection on geo for cross-filtering, d3 projections (Equal Earth, China Albers, Pacific-centred) and the map↔bar morph. China maps need a 审图号 (map review number) for PRC audiences. The DataV/AMap GeoJSON used in most ECharts tutorials is licensed for learning only, and GADM is non-commercial. So: Natural Earth admin-1 (public domain) for global audiences; a licensed, reviewed base map or a tile-grid cartogram for PRC audiences. deck.gl 9.4 (575 KB gz) should be an optional lazy engine for 10k+ points or flows. kepler.gl, L7, Mapbox, Leaflet.VectorGrid (Beerware) and leaflet.minichart (GPL) are reference-only or avoid.

key_insights: ANTIMERIDIAN BUG (verified in 6 engines): world-atlas TopoJSON is stitched for spherical d3 rendering. Leaflet, MapLibre, deck.gl, OpenLayers, L7 and ECharts' default projection all draw horizontal streaks from Russia/Chukotka, Fiji and Antarctica. Fix: d3.geoProject(fc, d3.geoEquirectangular().scale(180/Math.PI).translate([0,0]).reflectY(true).precision(0)) removes all 7 jumps in 25 ms; better, cut once in the Python builder (antimeridian, Apache-2.0, or shapely).

WINDING RULE: d3, Plot and ECharts-with-d3-projection need raw spherical geometry. Feeding the planar-cut, reflected geometry into a d3 projection inverted 2 polygons and filled the whole globe. Keep raw and cut variants, and assert d3.geoArea(f) < 2π in tests.

world-atlas 2.0.2 is archived and on Natural Earth 4.1.0. Its 110m file has no Singapore, Hong Kong, Macao, Bahrain, Malta, Cayman or Bermuda, the key financial centres for a bank. Natural Earth 5.1.2 10m simplified 1% keep-shapes is about the same size (109 KB raw / 36 KB gz) and keeps them.

Natural Earth ISO gotcha: ISO_A3/ISO_N3 are -99 for France and Norway (plus N. Cyprus, Somaliland, Kosovo); join on ISO_A3_EH or ADM0_A3. NE admin-0 also carries NAME_ZH/NAME_ZHT and 33 FCLASS_* worldview columns.

Natural Earth 5.x point-of-view variants (31 worldviews incl. China): ne_10m_admin_0_countries_chn merges Taiwan into China, keeps HK/Macao separate with SOVEREIGNT=China, and has a 9-dash-line indicator layer. Defaults are de facto boundaries.

Leaflet without tile layers: map.getMaxZoom() is Infinity. markercluster throws 'Map has no maxZoom specified', and leaflet.heat divides intensity by 2^12 (faint heat). Always set minZoom/maxZoom (kit geo-heat already resets heat maxZoom to the fitted zoom).

Leaflet 2.0 is still alpha.1 (Aug 2025), with no beta/rc 14+ months after the first alpha. leaflet-global.js still sets window.L, but factories are removed, so 1.x plugins break. The V1 polyfill fixed heat and markercluster but not ant-path ('Class constructor cannot be invoked without new'). Stay on 1.9.4 and write constructor-style, 2.0-ready code.

MapLibre GL JS 6.0 (2026-07-22) is ESM-only and WebGL2-only, with a module worker, and is blocked by CORS on file://. 5.24.0 is the last UMD and works offline: inline style + GeoJSON, in-memory PMTiles via addProtocol, and labels drawn with local fonts when glyph PBF fetches fail.

file:// rules: fetch/XHR, ES modules and module workers are blocked; blob workers and tiles from relative folders work (local raster tiles verified). Geo data must ship as classic JS (RK.geo.register). PMTiles works only through a custom in-memory Source over a base64-embedded buffer, verified in both protomaps-leaflet and MapLibre 5.

Offline network audit with requests blocked: Leaflet, ECharts, deck.gl, OpenLayers, Plot, MapLibre 5 and PMTiles made 0 external requests. AntV L7 made 1 (logo from gw.alipayobjects.com), fixed with logoVisible:false. This matters for confidentiality and for clients behind proxies.

ECharts 6.1 geo features verified offline: pie series with coordinateSystem:'geo' (replaces GPL leaflet.minichart), heatmap on geo, brush (rect/polygon) on geo with brushSelected data indices for cross-filtering, SVG renderer (heatmap becomes one raster <image>), projection.stream with d3 Equal Earth/conic/rotate for Pacific-centred or equal-area maps, registerMap specialAreas for insets, and the official 'Morphing between Map and Bar' example.

Licence red flags: leaflet.minichart GPL-2.0+; world-geojson GPL-3.0; Leaflet.VectorGrid Beerware; leaflet.pattern has no licence; Mapbox GL JS v2+ proprietary; DataV.GeoAtlas data is 'learning use only' (from 高德); GADM bans commercial use and redistribution; geoBoundaries is CC BY 4.0; Protomaps/OSM tiles are ODbL (attribution; review distribution of extracts).

Tile policies: the OSM tile server forbids offline use and bulk prefetch and may withdraw commercial access at any time; CARTO basemaps need an Enterprise licence for commercial use (free key = 5M tiles/month, non-commercial intent). Never default to online tiles; vector Natural Earth basemaps in theme colours look more 'pitchbook' anyway.

China compliance: publicly shown China maps need a 审图号. The 自然资源部 标准地图 can be used unmodified with its number, but cropping or zooming requires review. Microsoft suspended Excel map charts for China users. For PRC audiences, use a licensed or reviewed base, or a tile-grid cartogram (with Taiwan/HK/Macao tiles); Natural Earth admin-1 (32 CHN features with name_zh, iso_3166_2) suits global audiences only.

China province projection: d3.geoConicEqualArea().parallels([25,47]).rotate([-105,0]) through ECharts projection hooks, or Proj4Leaflet '+proj=aea +lat_1=25 +lat_2=47 +lon_0=105'. Join on GB/T 2260 adcodes (province-city-china, MIT) or ISO 3166-2:CN letter codes (CN-BJ).

Flow maps: avoid great-circle plugins (Leaflet.Arc wraps at the date line). Use quadratic Bézier SVG arcs with width ∝ value, arrowheads (direction survives print), node circles sized by in+out flow, and top-N aggregation above ~60 flows. For Americas–Asia flows a Pacific-centred view (ECharts + d3 rotate([-150,0])) reads better.

Bubbles: use L.circleMarker (pixel radius) not L.circle (metres); sqrt area scale; draw largest first; nested-circle legend; Leaflet draws circleMarkers as <path>, so animate radius with rAF tweens, not CSS r transitions.

Density: prefer hexbin (quantitative legend, crisp print) over blur heatmaps in pitchbooks; leaflet.heat and ECharts heatmaps are relative and raster. Use deck.gl HexagonLayer/HeatmapLayer (GPU) for 100k+ points.

Print: SVG engines (Leaflet SVG, ECharts SVG, Plot) print as vectors; WebGL/canvas engines (deck, MapLibre, L7, OL, Leaflet canvas, heatmaps) print as rasters. Hide zoom controls in print and call invalidateSize on beforeprint.

Leaflet in long reports: disable scrollWheelZoom or use gesture handling (leaflet-gesture-handling, MIT); call map.invalidateSize() from a ResizeObserver for maps in hidden tabs or collapsed sections.
